plugins.//: Bake the build identity into the package (issue #925). prepareCmd runs in semantic-release's prepare step — AFTER @semantic-release/npm bumps package.json to ${nextRelease.version} and BEFORE it packs/publishes the tarball — so the published package ships build-info.json and an npm-installed instance (no .git, no env override) can still report its gitSha. The recorded gitSha is the SOURCE HEAD the release is cut from; the tag commit is created afterwards by @semantic-release/git (see scripts/write-build-info.ts). There is deliberately NO verifyConditionsCmd: semantic-release runs verifyConditions BEFORE it computes nextRelease, so ${nextRelease.version} interpolates empty there and the command would fail with EVERIFYCONDITIONS, blocking every release. The workflow's OIDC-retry step re-runs plain `npm publish` (which re-packs) in the same checkout — where prepare already wrote build-info.json — and re-bakes it from package.json first (see release.yml), so the retry never publishes a tarball with no build-info.json.
